question: does a nonlinear unsupervised latent (GPLVM) give the image lag a home the linear factor model denies it?
RETRACTION: the first version of this analysis reported ARD relevance 0.464 for the lag against 0.188-0.204 for three nulls, and called the controls clean. THE CONTROL WAS CIRCULAR: the latent had been fitted with the true lag as one of its 26 outputs, so a smooth low-lengthscale direction existed for the lag by construction, while the nulls had never influenced the latent. I had diagnosed exactly this circularity for the predictive arm and failed to apply it to the ARD arm. Both arms are re-run below.

ARD_noncircular.design: latent fitted on the 25 TABULAR outputs only; ARD lengthscales then fitted for the lag and three nulls on that same lag-free latent, so all four are equally unseen
ARD_noncircular.verdict: NULL. On a lag-free latent the lag reaches 0.205 against nulls at 0.175-0.241 -- it is INSIDE the null range, and noise_lagcov (0.241) beats it. The entire 0.46-vs-0.19 separation was the circularity.

predictive_clean_refit.design: latent refitted from scratch on the 25 tabular outputs, three independent initialisations, lag predicted out of fold

superseded.defect: latent initialised from a fit that had seen the lag

predictive_clean_refit.verdict: the 0.040 does not survive. FA-init gives 0.036, PCA-init 0.034, and RANDOM init gives -0.002. The two informative inits land on the linear FA latent's own value (0.033) and ridge on raw tabular (0.032) -- i.e. the GPLVM recovers the LINEAR signal and adds nothing. The random-init collapse shows the apparent gain was inherited from the linear initialisation, not learned.

CONCLUSION: NULL, after removing two layers of circularity. A nonlinear unsupervised latent does NOT give the image lag a home the linear model denies it. ARD relevance is inside the null band; predictive R2 matches the linear latent when initialised informatively and vanishes when initialised randomly. Combined with the earlier supervised results (A: magnitude hypothesis rejected; B: no interactions; C: nonlinear detection floor ~0.10 at n=883), the lag's near-independence is a property of the DATA, not an artefact of assuming linearity.
variational_decision: the planned Bayesian GPLVM is NOT worth building. Its purpose was to attach posterior widths to a signal that, on this evidence, is not there. The from-scratch refit was the right gate and it closed.
caveats: MAP GPLVM, Q=8, 250 Adam steps, single restart per initialisation -- a longer or multi-restart fit could differ, though the random-init collapse is hard to attribute to optimisation alone
the nonlinear detection floor measured earlier (~R2 0.10 at n=883) applies here too: an effect smaller than that would be invisible to this method as well
